learning_outcomes.text: Be able to solve problems related to electrical circuits and machines.
Be able to write a technical report on a project in the field of electrotechnics that includes a calculation part and an experimental part.
Be able to solve three-phase systems.
Be able to solve simple magnetic circuits.
Be able to solve electrical circuits powered by direct current and alternating current.
Be able to describe and analyze electrical systems that include electrical machines among their components.

syllabus_topics: Power and energy: conservation of power
Power entering a dipole. Instantaneous, active, and fluctuating power. Power factor
Apparent power and reactive power. Complex power
Power and energy in basic elements
Relationship between line and phase values
Measurement of active power in three-phase systems
Measurement of reactive power in three-phase systems
Magnetic circuits: analogy with electrical circuits
Energy losses in a ferromagnetic core
Basic measurements in circuits. Multimeters and power supplies
Analysis of circuits in sinusoidal steady state
Power measurement in circuits in sinusoidal steady state
teaching_methods: Laboratory practical work (assembly of electrical elements and circuits, measurement and analysis of electrical quantities)

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment: In-course written theoretical-practical tests

assessment_rules: To pass, students must achieve an overall average grade of at least 5 out of 10. For the first call, the final exam accounts for 70% (minimum 4/10) and continuous assessment for 30%. Continuous assessment includes laboratory practical work (10%, no minimum) and in-course written tests (20%, no minimum). If the minimum grade for the final exam is not met, the final course grade will be the exam grade. In the second call, the final exam accounts for 90% (minimum 4/10) and laboratory practical work for 10% (no minimum), with the repetition of partial exams included in the final exam. Laboratory practical work is not recoverable.
